title: Quaint Smoky Argentinian Beef Empanadas
description: Spicy and festive Argentinian dish featuring ground cinnamon and smoky heat, these empanadas are perfect for any occasion. They are also FODMAP friendly.
instructions: In a large skillet, cook the ground beef over medium-high heat until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion, minced garlic, ground cinnamon, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper to the skillet and cook until the onion is translucent.
Allow the beef mixture to cool to room temperature.
Roll out the empanada dough to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Use a cookie cutter or the rim of a glass to cut out circles of dough.
Place a tablespoon or two of the beef mixture onto the center of each dough circle.
Fold the dough in half over the filling and press the edges together to seal the empanada.
Brush the tops of the empanadas with the beaten egg for a golden glaze.
Place the empanadas on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
